A complete guide to using the scan feature to identify breeds in your cattle.

How to Scan

Open SapiKenal and make sure you are on the Scan tab. Point the camera at the cattle you want to examine.

Tips for Taking Good Photos

• Prioritize a close-up photo of the symptom area (mouth, hooves, or skin)
• Make sure the symptom area fills most of the frame and is clearly visible
• Ensure adequate lighting and avoid shadows on the symptom area
• Position the camera level with the symptom area, not from above
• Avoid blurry, too distant, or obstructed images

After Taking a Photo

The app will process the image and display the classification result within seconds. Results include the predicted class, confidence score, and handling recommendations.

You can also select an image from your gallery by tapping the gallery icon at the bottom of the camera screen.
Differences between online and offline inference modes, and when to use each.

Online Mode

In online mode, the image is sent to the server for analysis using the full MobileNetV3 model. This mode requires a stable internet connection.

Online mode advantages:
• Higher accuracy using the full server-side model
• Automatic model updates without needing to update the app

Offline Mode

In offline mode, analysis is performed directly on your device using TensorFlow Lite. This mode works without an internet connection.

Offline mode advantages:
• Works in locations without internet signal
• Faster processing since no data is sent to the server
• Image data stays on your device (more private)

When to Use Each?

Use online mode when you have a stable internet connection and need the highest accuracy results. Use offline mode when in the field without signal or when you need instant results.

The app will automatically switch to offline mode if the server cannot be reached.
How to read confidence scores and understand the reliability of detection results.

Confidence Score

Every breed identification result includes a confidence score as a percentage. This score indicates the model confidence in the predicted breed.

Confidence Levels

• High (≥80%): The model is very confident in the result.
• Medium (60–79%): The model is fairly confident; rescan with a clearer photo or from a different angle.
• Low (<60%): The model is uncertain. Rescan with better photo conditions.

Per-Class Scores

Besides the main breed, the app displays scores for Bali, Brahman, Brangus, and Limousin. This helps you see the distribution of model output scores.

When to Rescan?

• Confidence score below 60%
• Photo taken was blurry or poorly lit
• Result does not match the visible cattle characteristics

Important: Results from this app are an image classification aid, not a substitute for expert livestock assessment.
Visual characteristics that help distinguish Bali cattle in an image.

Bali cattle are a local Indonesian breed commonly recognized by a compact body, a distinctive coat, and a dark line along the back. Color and body shape can vary with age, sex, and management.\n\nFor a useful image, capture the whole side of the animal in clear, even light. Use this guide together with the model scores; a photo alone is not a pedigree certificate.
Coat, proportions, and visible structure to review during identification.

Look for the overall combination rather than one isolated feature:
• Compact proportions and a moderate frame
• A coat that may range from reddish brown to dark brown depending on sex and age
• A darker dorsal line and darker lower legs are common visual clues
• A light rump area may be visible in some animals

Keep the camera level with the animal and avoid cropped legs, heavy shadows, or obstructing objects.
A practical checklist for consistent image-based comparison.

Before comparing a photo, check the same cues across all candidates:
• Side angle with the body fully visible
• Neutral posture on level ground
• Even lighting without a strong color cast
• Enough detail to inspect the coat and back line

Review the Bali score alongside the other three class scores. If the scores are close, treat the result as uncertain and capture another angle.
How to combine the profile, image quality, and model confidence.

Use the profile as supporting information for breed identification. Confirm important decisions with farm records or a qualified livestock professional.\n\nA clear image can still produce an uncertain classification. Retake the photo when the animal is too small, blurred, poorly lit, or partly hidden. Never treat a model result as proof of lineage or registration.
Visual characteristics that help distinguish Brahman cattle in an image.

Brahman cattle are known for a prominent shoulder hump, loose skin, and long ears. Coat colors commonly range from light gray to red, and individual appearance varies with age and management.\n\nFor a useful image, capture the whole side of the animal and include the shoulder, head, and ears. Use the profile with the model scores; an image result is not proof of pedigree.
Coat, proportions, and visible structure to review during identification.

Review the combination of visible cues:
• A defined hump over the shoulders
• Loose skin under the neck and along the body
• Long, drooping ears and a relatively long face
• Light gray, silver, or red coat variations

Keep the camera level with the animal. Avoid cropped ears, heavy shadows, and poses that hide the shoulder profile.
A practical checklist for consistent image-based comparison.

Use consistent framing when comparing photos:
• Show the full body from a side or three-quarter angle
• Keep the head and shoulder hump visible
• Use even lighting and a neutral background
• Compare the same features across candidate animals

Review the Brahman score with the other three class scores. Close scores indicate that another clear photo may help.

Visual characteristics that help distinguish Brangus cattle in an image.

Brangus cattle commonly have a black coat, a muscular body, and features combining Brahman and Angus characteristics. Individual appearance varies with age, sex, and management.\n\nCapture the whole side of the animal in even light. Use this profile together with the model scores; an image result is not proof of pedigree.
Coat, proportions, and visible structure to review during identification.

Review the combination of visible cues:
• A black or very dark coat is common
• A muscular body with a strong back and hindquarters
• Ears may show the longer character associated with Brahman influence
• Skin and shoulder shape may show Brahman influence

Avoid lighting that removes detail from the dark coat. Include the head, shoulder, and legs when possible.
Visual characteristics that help distinguish Limousin cattle in an image.

Limousin cattle commonly have a golden-red to reddish-brown coat, a muscular body, and strong hindquarters. Individual appearance varies with age, sex, and management.\n\nCapture the whole side of the animal in even light. Use this profile together with the model scores; an image result is not proof of pedigree.
Coat, proportions, and visible structure to review during identification.

Review the combination of visible cues:
• A characteristic golden-red or reddish-brown coat
• A muscular body with a developed chest and hindquarters
• The muzzle and area around the eyes may appear lighter
• Strong legs with a balanced posture

Use a side or three-quarter angle with the head, shoulder, and legs visible. Retake the photo if shadows hide the color or structure.
